input.prompt:
Research task, no code changes. Marcel wants the ZimmProductCard live homepage demo (overrides/app/pages/home/liveProductCardDemoSection.tsx, branch feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo) to show EVERY variant/state prescribed by SFCC-236's real ACs + Figma designs + Jira comment thread — not the current curated 11 instances. He explicitly wants them organized under 5 categories: Core component, PLP, Home, Wishlist, Recently Viewed.

Do this:

1. Fetch the live SFCC-236 Jira ticket (description/ACs AND every comment, not from memory or prior session summaries) via whatever Atlassian/Jira tool is available (ToolSearch for it if you don't already have it loaded). Read the ACs verbatim. Check specifically whether they're literally grouped under headings matching Core component / PLP / Home / Wishlist / Recently Viewed — if so, use that exact structure; if not, infer the closest mapping and say explicitly that you inferred it.

2. Read ~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-236/plan.md, findings.md, handoff.md, and postbuild.md — these are this exact build's own planning/audit artifacts from earlier in this project and likely already contain a real AC-to-Figma-node cross-reference from the "final wrap-up" audit round (zimmerMANNPostBuild skill) that ran on this ticket. Use them as a head start, not a substitute for re-checking the live Jira ticket and live Figma nodes yourself.

3. Check the real, live Figma nodes for ZimmProductCard / ZimmProductCardMedia / ZimmProductCardContent. The component source files cite their own originating Figma node IDs in docblock comments — e.g. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx` cites "Figma 'Image Group' component set, node 40002742:46323"; grep the other component files (`zimmProductCard/index.tsx`, `zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx`, and any `.css.ts` recipe files in that family) for their own cited node IDs too. Before calling any Figma MCP tool, load the design-to-code skill guidance first (its own tool description requires this — use the Skill tool for "figma-design-to-code" or read the skill://figma/figma-design-to-code/SKILL.md resource). Use get_metadata and/or get_design_context on those exact nodes to see every variant/state Figma actually defines (variant properties — e.g. size/type/state combinations) for this component family, not just what's already been built into code.

4. Read the FULL current `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx` (don't rely on a partial/truncated prior read — re-read the whole file now), plus `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/index.stories.tsx` and `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.stories.tsx`. Build an exact inventory of every variant/state ALREADY implemented/exercised ANYWHERE in this component family's Storybook coverage (not just the 11 currently shown in the homepage demo) — include each story's exact prop/arg combination.

5. Cross-reference all of the above into ONE master list: every genuinely distinct variant/state the real ACs + Figma + Jira comments require, grouped under the 5 categories Marcel named (Core component / PLP / Home / Wishlist / Recently Viewed). For each entry give: category, a short descriptive name, the exact prop/state combination needed to render it as concretely as possible (e.g. "isUnavailable: true + onNotifyMe present", "images.length > 1 for multi-image gallery", "originalPrice set alongside currentPrice for Was/Now"), and its source (AC number, Figma node/variant name, or a quoted Jira comment). Mark each entry as either already covered by the current 11 demo instances, covered elsewhere in Storybook but missing from the demo, or not implemented anywhere yet.

6. Flag explicitly and separately: (a) anything in the ACs/Figma/comments that ZimmProductCard's real, current prop API (the organism-level `ZimmProductCardProps` discriminated union — check `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx` for the real current shape) cannot actually express today, i.e. a genuine spec-vs-implementation gap, not just "missing from the demo"; (b) anything genuinely ambiguous or contradictory between the three sources (ACs vs Figma vs Jira comments).

Do NOT write or edit any code — this is pure research and reporting. Report back the full master list (grouped by the 5 categories, one row per variant/state, with its coverage status and source), plus the gap list and the ambiguity list. Be thorough and complete — this list is what gets implemented in the demo next, so a missed variant here is a missed variant in the final output. Keep the report well-organized (tables per category are fine) but don't pad it with narrative — Marcel and I both want the factual list, not commentary.

Executes an approved zimmerMANNPreBuild plan through a closed-loop multi-agent workflow — implement, test, scope-check, score, rework until passed — committing each step and handing off to zimmerMANNPostBuild. Also handles rework from CodeRabbit or reviewer change requests after a PR is open.

Reads the session transcripts and run artefacts for named stories, diagnoses where the loop failed and whose gap it was, checks whether the skills still cite things that are true, and proposes concrete edits to the build skills and loop agents — applied only on Marcel's explicit go.

Gathers and cross-checks every source — Jira, Confluence, the FED handbook, the codebase and Figma — flags every gap and misalignment, then produces an executable closed-loop build plan and hands off to zimmerMANNBuild. Use at the start of any story, ticket or build task.

1	import React from 'react';
2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	import { defineMessages, useIntl } from 'react-intl';
4	import { ZimmProductCardMedia } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardMedia';
5	import type { ZimmProductCardMediaImage } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardMedia';
6	import { ZimmProductCardContent } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardContent';
7	import type { ZimmSizeChipValue } from '../../molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup';
8	
9	/**
10	 * SFCC-236 Step 6 — the organism that assembles Step 4's `ZimmProductCardMedia` and Step 5's
11	 * `ZimmProductCardContent` into the full product card, across the three confirmed variations.
12	 * Figma component set `Product-card`, node `40000223:2822` (20 variants: Size x State x Type x
13	 * Unavailable), file `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm`. The variation matrix below reflects the resolved
14	 * `hidden`-attribute reading confirmed against the real assembled Card-content instances:
15	 *
16	 *   Home      (40000214:6141 default / 40002163:36593 hover)   — image + name only by default;
17	 *             bag/attributes/size-selector hidden always; a hover-CAPABLE pointer reveals price
18	 *             on hover. Mobile (`40000223:2821`) shows price unconditionally instead — it has no
19	 *             Hover variant at all, so a price hidden "by default, revealed on hover" like the
20	 *             original build shipped would never be revealed there at all (Fix E, found in the
21	 *             full-sweep follow-up audit; confirmed live as a real bug, not just a Figma reading).
22	 *             Arrows appear on hover-capable pointers regardless of variation (Media's own
23	 *             concern, driven purely by image count).
24	 *   PLP/PDP   (40002163:41441 default / 40002163:41459 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
25	 *             price by default, no attributes, size-selector hidden; hover hides price and
26	 *             reveals the size-selector in its place; arrows appear.
27	 *   Wishlist  (40002187:58446 default / 40002187:58458 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
28	 *             attributes (colour+size) + price by default, size-selector hidden; hover hides
29	 *             price and reveals the size-selector, confirmed identical to PLP's own hover reveal
30	 *             via node `40002187:58460` (the Wishlist hover instance carries no `hidden`
31	 *             attribute on "Size Selector" at all) — this is NOT what the SFCC-236 Jira AC text
32	 *             says (it only mentions the image switch + arrows for Wishlist hover). It shipped
33	 *             matching the design anyway — a judgment call made during implementation, not a
34	 *             conflict that was raised on the ticket or separately ratified.
35	 *
36	 * "Recently Viewed Full History" is not a fourth variation — the AC states it behaves exactly
37	 * like PLP, so callers pass `variation: 'plp'` for it.
38	 *
39	 * Unavailable=True (Fix C, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) is confirmed designed for **every**
40	 * variation, not just `plp` — an earlier revision of this paragraph claimed the opposite, before
41	 * the Default+Hover Unavailable instances for `home` (40002163:39981 / :39990) and `wishlist`
42	 * (40002187:58452 / :58464) were actually checked. The confirmed rule, identical across all three:
43	 *   - The PLP/Wishlist size-selector hover-swap is suppressed entirely when unavailable — nothing
44	 *     to pick for an out-of-stock item, so price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced
45	 *     (`hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector` are both AND-ed with `!isUnavailable` below).
46	 *     Home's own hover-reveals-price behaviour is unaffected — its Unavailable Hover reference
47	 *     still reveals price exactly as the in-stock case does.
48	 *   - "Notify me" is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default, revealed on
49	 *     hover/focus-visible, confirmed via every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference) but
50	 *     unconditionally visible on touch (confirmed via the Mobile Unavailable references —
51	 *     Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so whatever they show is the only state a touch
52	 *     pointer ever sees, and all of them show notify-me plainly).
53	 * `isUnavailable` and `onNotifyMe` are threaded through uniformly to `ZimmProductCardContent`
54	 * (the only one of the two composed children with an `isUnavailable` concept at all —
55	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia` has no such prop); this organism does not itself restrict `showNotifyMe`
56	 * to any one variation — a caller that never passes `onNotifyMe` simply gets no notify-me button.
57	 *
58	 * Fix F (full-sweep follow-up audit, after the above was already built and approved): the
59	 * Desktop-only "price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover" behaviour above is NOT what
60	 * Mobile does. Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`) both have

143	 * colour/size attributes, price, PLP-only size-chip picker, and an out-of-stock notify-me CTA.

145	 * 40002163:37103).

147	 * Deliberately has NO remove/close button — that action lives entirely in
148	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `close` overlay (Step 4), positioned on the image, not here.
149	 *
150	 * Also deliberately has no badge slot, despite the SFCC-236 AC mentioning one for PLP/Wishlist.

164	  headingLevel,
165	  href,
166	  currentPrice,
167	  originalPrice,
168	  isPriceLoading,
169	  showAttributes,
170	  colour,
171	  size,
172	  showBag,
173	  isUnavailable,
174	  onAddToBag,
175	  showSizeChips,

183	  // `disabled`, not `isUnavailable` — matches `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s own `DEFAULT_STYLE_PROPS`

185	  // false branch of `bagButton`'s disabled styling (see zimmProductCardContent.css.ts's own
186	  // comment, and `zimmSizeChip.css.ts`'s identical `disabled` naming for the same reason).
187	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_CONTENT_RECIPE, { disabled: isUnavailable });
188	
189	  // Both conditions required, matching the component contract exactly — not just `showNotifyMe`
190	  // alone, so an organism that sets the flag without wiring a real callback silently renders
191	  // nothing rather than an inert button.
192	  const showNotifyMeButton = showNotifyMe && Boolean(onNotifyMe);
193	
194	  // Figma renders the colour/size attributes line as ONE continuous phrase, not two independent
195	  // labels: the comma is baked into the colour text node's own content ("Lilac Sand,"), not a
196	  // separate punctuation element — confirmed via get_design_context on node 40002187:58446 (the
197	  // real Wishlist Card-content instance). Reproduced the same way here, on the colour value's own
198	  // rendered string (never as a static comma JSX node between the two spans), paired with
199	  // attributesRow's 2px gap (zimmProductCardContent.css.ts) for the "Ivory, M" breathing room —
200	  // verified by rendering the real Futura Round Medium caption style at actual size: the glyph
201	  // ink-to-ink gap the 2px flex gap produces here reads as a genuine (if slightly tighter than
202	  // full-prose) space, not as "Ivory,M" touching. Guarded against `colour` being falsy so a
203	  // caller omitting it (a contract violation, but not this component's job to enforce) still
204	  // renders nothing, rather than the literal string "undefined,".
205	  const colourWithComma = colour ? `${colour},` : colour;
206	
207	  return (
208	    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.content}>
209	      <chakra.div __css={styles.nameRow}>
210	        <ProductNameLink to={href} __css={styles.nameLink}>
211	          <ZimmProductName name={name} as={headingLevel} />
212	        </ProductNameLink>
213	
214	        {showBag && (
215	          <chakra.div __css={styles.bagWrapper} data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.bag}>
216	            <chakra.button
217	              type="button"
218	              __css={styles.bagButton}
219	              aria-label={intl.formatMessage(messages.addToBag)}
220	              disabled={isUnavailable}
221	              onClick={() => {

223	                // from ever dispatching this click, but stating the invariant explicitly means a
224	                // reader doesn't have to recall that fact to trust onAddToBag can't fire while
225	                // unavailable. Same idiom as ZimmSizeChip's own onClick guard.
226	                if (isUnavailable) return;

232	          </chakra.div>
233	        )}

236	      {showAttributes && (

238	          <chakra.span __css={styles.colourText}>{colourWithComma}</chakra.span>
239	          <chakra.span __css={styles.sizeText}>{size}</chakra.span>
240	        </chakra.div>
241	      )}
242	
243	      <chakra.div __css={styles.priceWrapper} data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.price}>
244	        <ZimmProductPrice
245	          currentPrice={currentPrice}
246	          originalPrice={originalPrice}
247	          isLoading={isPriceLoading}
248	          isLive={false}

250	      </chakra.div>

252	      {showSizeChips && (
253	        <chakra.div __css={styles.sizeChipWrapper} data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}>
254	          <ZimmSizeChipGroup

256	            selectedValue={selectedSizeChipValue}
257	            onSelect={onSizeChipSelect}
258	          />
259	        </chakra.div>
260	      )}
261	
262	      {showNotifyMeButton && (
263	        <chakra.button
264	          type="button"
265	          __css={styles.notifyMeButton}
266	          onClick={onNotifyMe}
267	          data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}
268	        >
269	          {intl.formatMessage(messages.notifyMe)}

271	      )}
272	    </chakra.div>
273	  );
274	};

93	 *          z-index:auto participant one level up — and, being earlier in DOM order than
94	 *          `[data-card-slot="content"]`, it lost. Moving the lift to the `carousel` WRAPPER itself
95	 *          (already `position: absolute` from Media's own recipe, so only `zIndex: 1` is needed
96	 *          here, same as `close`) fixes this: the wrapper's own stacking context — not one buried
97	 *          inside it — is what gets compared against the overlay, and it wins outright, carrying
98	 *          both arrow buttons above the overlay with it. This is exactly the gap
99	 *          index.test.tsx's own "KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock warns about — jsdom resolves no
100	 *          stacking contexts at all, so this shipped past every automated check and was only
101	 *          found by a real click in a real browser. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 3" describe block.
102	 *   3. THE HOVER-REVEAL SWAP between price and the PLP/Wishlist size-selector (and Home's
103	 *      hidden-by-default price), gated by the same `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` query
104	 *      `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already uses for its own arrows/indicator split. Each reveal
105	 *      rule fires on `:hover` OR `:has(:focus-visible)` on this same root (Fix 2 rework below,
106	 *      superseded by Fix H — see point 6) — `:hover` alone would leave every reveal permanently
107	 *      unreachable by keyboard on a hover-capable device, since `display: none` removes the
108	 *      unconditional-state element from the tab order entirely and nothing but a real pointer
109	 *      hover could ever have revealed it.
110	 *   4. NOTIFY-ME'S HOVER GATE (Fix C, found during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit against the
111	 *      real Figma Default+Hover Unavailable instances for all three variations, desktop AND
112	 *      mobile). Three behaviours confirmed together, all different from point 3 above:
113	 *        - `isUnavailable` suppresses the PLP/Wishlist size-selector swap entirely (index.tsx
114	 *          AND-s `hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector` with `!isUnavailable` before they
115	 *          ever reach this recipe) — there is nothing to pick for an out-of-stock item, so price
116	 *          stays visible on hover instead of being replaced. Home's own `hoverRevealsPrice` is
117	 *          untouched by this — its Unavailable Hover reference still reveals price normally.
118	 *        - Suppressing that swap is not, by itself, enough to reproduce the reference: with no
119	 *          hide/reveal pair of its own, the size-chip wrapper falls back to Content's natural
120	 *          (visible) default and would show permanently — briefly shipped exactly that way mid-fix
121	 *          and caught by re-checking the real render against Figma, which shows size chips hidden
122	 *          in BOTH states when unavailable, not merely "not swapped in on hover". `sizeSelectorUnavailable`
123	 *          (index.tsx: `config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && isUnavailable`) carries that permanent
124	 *          hide as its own unconditional rule below — deliberately outside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`
125	 *          entirely, since unlike everything else here this isn't a pointer-type distinction at
126	 *          all: every device sees it hidden, full stop.
127	 *        - Notify-me itself is hover-gated the OPPOSITE way round from price/the size-selector:
128	 *          hidden by default and revealed on hover **only inside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`**, not
129	 *          unconditionally. Every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference shows it appearing only on
130	 *          hover; every Mobile Unavailable reference (Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so
131	 *          whatever it shows is the only state a touch pointer ever sees) shows it plainly with no
132	 *          reveal needed. Putting the "hidden by default" half outside the media query — matching
133	 *          point 3's own structure literally — would have made notify-me permanently invisible on
134	 *          touch, since a touch pointer never matches `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` and so could never
135	 *          trigger the `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` half either.
136	 *   5. THE BAG ICON'S PLP-ONLY MOBILE HIDE (Fix D, same SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit). A genuinely
137	 *      different axis from points 3-4 above: `DESKTOP_QUERY` is a **viewport-width** media query
138	 *      (`min-width`), not `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`'s pointer-capability one — a large touch tablet and
139	 *      a small hover-capable laptop window need to agree with Figma's own Desktop/Mobile split by
140	 *      width, not by input method. Figma's PLP/PDP Mobile Card-content instance
141	 *      (`40002163:41479`) has the bag icon's `Icons` frame `hidden="true"`; Desktop's own PLP
142	 *      instance and Wishlist's Mobile instance (`40002187:58472`) both leave it visible — so this
143	 *      is `hideBagOnMobile`, one boolean `index.tsx` derives from TWO separate per-variation
144	 *      config fields (`hideBagOnMobile` proper, PLP's own unconditional rule; and
145	 *      `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable`, Fix G's narrower Wishlist-only-when-out-of-stock rule —
146	 *      see index.tsx's own docblock and `bagHiddenOnMobile` derivation), not a blanket rule. This
147	 *      recipe only ever sees the one already-combined boolean — it has no opinion on which of the
148	 *      two reasons produced it. Hidden unconditionally by default (mobile-first, matching
149	 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`'s own padding step direction), then shown again from
150	 *      `DESKTOP_QUERY` up as `display: 'flex'` — not `'block'` — since that is the actual display
151	 *      type `bagWrapper`'s own recipe uses for its icon-centring; this selector's specificity
152	 *      (a class + two attribute selectors) beats Content's single class either way, so restoring
153	 *      the wrong display value would have silently flattened that centring rather than merely
154	 *      failing to apply — the inverse of point 3's hover-reveal shape, but the same "start from
155	 *      the narrowest/most restrictive case, widen from there" idea.
156	 *   6. THE CAROUSEL ARROW REVEAL (behavioural fix, confirmed against the Jira AC — "when on
157	 *      desktop and the user hovers, then the arrows appear" — and live Figma: the Carousel
158	 *      element is `hidden="true"` on every Default-state instance checked and visible only on
159	 *      the matching Hover-state instance, for both PLP and Wishlist). Unlike points 3-4 above,
160	 *      this reveal is **unconditional** inside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` — not gated behind a
161	 *      `ZimmProductCardStyleProps` flag — because the arrows behave identically across every
162	 *      variation (Home/PLP/Wishlist) whenever a card has more than one image; there is no
163	 *      `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry for it and this fix does not add one. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s
164	 *      own `carousel` part used to reveal itself unconditionally inside its own
165	 *      `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` block — a device-CAPABILITY check, not an actual-hover check —
166	 *      which made the arrows visible permanently on any hover-capable device instead of only
167	 *      while genuinely hovering/focusing the card. That sub-block is now removed entirely from
168	 *      `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`; the `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` pair here is the only
169	 *      reveal path left, the same mechanism point 3 already established for price/the size-selector.
170	 *      Purely additive to the existing `carousel` z-index lift in point 2 above — that lift
171	 *      already handles stacking once the arrows are visible; this handles visibility itself.
172	 *
173	 *      Fix H (live-browser check immediately after the above shipped): clicking an arrow button
174	 *      gives it real DOM focus in every evergreen engine, which kept the then-`:focus-within`
175	 *      reveal true — and the arrows visible — even after the mouse moved back out, until focus
176	 *      moved elsewhere entirely (confirmed live: arrows stayed up until a click landed outside
177	 *      the card). The same shared-root `:focus-within` shape underlies every reveal in point 3
178	 *      too (price, the size-selector, notify-me), so a click on a size chip or the notify-me
179	 *      button reproduces the identical stuck-open symptom — this fix was therefore applied to
180	 *      every `:focus-within` occurrence in this recipe, not just this one. `:has(:focus-visible)`
181	 *      replaces `:focus-within` everywhere in this file: it matches only when the browser's own
182	 *      heuristic says a keyboard focus ring is warranted, which a mouse-click-focused `<button>`
183	 *      never satisfies in any evergreen engine, while genuine Tab navigation still does — so
184	 *      keyboard parity (Fix 2's original reason for adding a focus-based reveal at all) is fully
185	 *      preserved, and the mouse-click case is not. `:has()` is new to this codebase as of this
186	 *      fix; it is fully covered by this project's own browserslist (`iOS >= 17`, `Android >= 14`,
187	 *      `last 4 ChromeAndroid versions`), all far past `:has()`'s 2022/2023 shipping baseline.
188	 *
189	 * Parts: only `root` is declared. Everything above is a nested descendant selector inside
190	 * `root`'s own style object (targeting the composed children's `data-card-slot` attributes), not
191	 * a separate Chakra part — `index.tsx` never reads anything off `useMultiStyleConfig` but
192	 * `styles.root`, so `recipeParts.test.ts`'s declared-vs-read reconciliation needs nothing more.
193	 *
194	 * `zIndex: 1` below is this file's one deliberately unnamed magic number — accepted per
195	 * .claude/rules/conventions.md's own exception ("0, 1, -1 in obvious idiomatic uses"): it is the
196	 * standard "one level above the default/auto stacking layer" value, used identically at each of
197	 * the three lift points, and the stretched-link overlay is deliberately left with no z-index of
198	 * its own rather than pinned to a specific lower number — so the two sides only ever need to be
199	 * *some* value vs a *higher* one, never a specific pair.
200	 */
201	export const ZimmProductCard = {
202	  parts: ['root'],
203	
204	  baseStyle: ({
205	    hoverHidesPrice,
206	    hoverRevealsPrice,
207	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector,
208	    hoverRevealsNotifyMe,
209	    sizeSelectorUnavailable,
210	    hideBagOnMobile,
211	  }: ZimmProductCardStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
212	    root: {
213	      position: 'relative',
214	      width: '100%',
215	
216	      // 1. Stretched-link overlay — see docblock point 1. Deliberately no z-index of its own
217	      // (stays at the default/auto stacking layer), so every control lifted in point 2 below
218	      // reliably paints above it regardless of DOM order.
219	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] a::after`]: {
220	        content: '""',
221	        position: 'absolute',
222	        inset: 0,
223	      },
224	
225	      // 2. Every genuinely-interactive control sits above the stretched overlay. A plain `button`
226	      // type-selector under the relevant data-card-slot root reaches every control uniformly —
227	      // none of them declare their own data-card-slot, and none needs one: Content's bag button,
228	      // its notify-me button, and every ZimmSizeChip button nested inside its own sizeChips
229	      // wrapper are all real <button> descendants of [data-card-slot="content"].
230	      // Fix 1 (Scorer rework round 1): NO position value here. ZimmProductCardMedia's own
231	      // `close` recipe part already sets `position: 'absolute', top: 0, right: 0` on this exact
232	      // element (that's how the remove button pins to the image's top-right corner). This rule's
233	      // `.css-root [data-card-slot="close"]` descendant+attribute selector has HIGHER
234	      // specificity than Media's own single-class rule, so a competing `position` value declared
235	      // here would win the cascade and knock the button out of its pinned position into normal
236	      // flow — which is exactly what shipped here before this fix. The element is already
237	      // positioned (by Media's own recipe), which is all `zIndex` needs to take effect; no
238	      // `position` re-declaration was ever necessary. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe
239	      // blocks for the object-shape and real-DOM/getComputedStyle proof.
240	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.close}"]`]: {
241	        zIndex: 1,
242	      },
243	      // Fix 3 — zIndex only, on the carousel WRAPPER, not on each arrow `button` inside it. See
244	      // docblock point 2 above for why lifting the buttons individually left them unclickable in
245	      // a real browser (a `transform`-induced stacking context on this wrapper trapped their own
246	      // zIndex) despite passing every jsdom test.
247	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
248	        zIndex: 1,
249	      },
250	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] button`]: {
251	        position: 'relative',
252	        zIndex: 1,
253	      },
254	
255	      // 3. Hover-reveal swap — see docblock point 3. The unconditional (outside-media-query)
256	      // half of each flag below is what makes a touch/no-hover pointer see the *default* state
257	      // permanently: it never matches HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY at all, so whichever rule fired outside
258	      // it (or the total absence of one) is the only state that pointer type ever sees.
259	      //
260	      // `hoverRevealsPrice` (Home) is deliberately NOT here, unlike `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`
261	      // below it — see Fix E in the [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY] block: Home's price must stay visible
262	      // unconditionally on a touch pointer, the opposite of what an unconditional hide here would
263	      // do.
264	      ...(hoverRevealsSizeSelector && {
265	        // PLP/Wishlist: size-selector starts hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type...
266	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
267	      }),
268	      // Fix C — see docblock point 4. Unconditional and permanent, on every device: an
269	      // out-of-stock item never gets the size-selector, in any state, so this is the only rule
270	      // for it at all when `sizeSelectorUnavailable` is true (no corresponding reveal exists
271	      // anywhere, inside or outside the media query below).
272	      ...(sizeSelectorUnavailable && {
273	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
274	        // Fix F (full-sweep follow-up audit): mobile-only price hide. Figma's Mobile PLP/Wishlist
275	        // Unavailable references hide price and show notify-me in its place — a genuine swap,
276	        // unlike Desktop's own additive treatment (price stays, notify-me is simply added on
277	        // hover, handled by hoverRevealsNotifyMe below). Hidden by default (mobile-first, matching
278	        // this file's own hideBagOnMobile direction); the DESKTOP_QUERY reveal lives in the single
279	        // shared [DESKTOP_QUERY] block below, NOT a second one here — see that block's own comment
280	        // for why a second `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object key at this level would silently clobber it.
281	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
282	      }),
283	
284	      [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: {
285	        ...(hoverRevealsPrice && {
286	          // Fix E (full-sweep follow-up audit): the "hidden by default" half moved IN HERE from
287	          // the unconditional block above, where it used to live — Home's Mobile reference
288	          // (40000223:2821) shows price plainly, and Mobile has no Hover variant at all to ever
289	          // reveal a price hidden unconditionally like the original shape did. Confirmed live as
290	          // a real, shipped bug (the Home story showed no price whatsoever at mobile widths), not
291	          // just a Figma reading. Same shape Fix C already established for notify-me, applied
292	          // here for the same underlying reason: a touch pointer must never see this half at all.
293	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
294	          // ...and is only revealed here, once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card.
295	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
296	            display: 'block',
297	          },
298	          // Fix 2 (Scorer rework round 1): `display: none` removes an element from the tab
299	          // order entirely, so a keyboard-only user on a hover-capable device (tabbing, not
300	          // hovering) could never reveal this via `:hover` alone. Originally `:focus-within` on
301	          // this same root — scoped here, not on the price/size-chip wrapper itself, so that
302	          // focus landing on ANY descendant control (name link, bag button, size chip) triggers
303	          // the reveal — mirroring zimmSearchInput.css.ts's container/zimmFormRow's own
304	          // `_focusWithin` sibling to `_hover`.
305	          // Fix H (live-browser check after the arrow reveal shipped): plain `:focus-within`
306	          // does not distinguish a real Tab-focused descendant from one that only has focus
307	          // because the user *clicked* it with a mouse — most browsers give a `<button>` real
308	          // DOM focus on click, so clicking any interactive control inside the card (an arrow,
309	          // a size chip, notify-me) left `:focus-within` true, and therefore every reveal below
310	          // stuck open, until focus moved elsewhere entirely (e.g. a click outside the card) —
311	          // moving the mouse back out was not enough. `:has(:focus-visible)` fixes this: it only
312	          // matches when the browser's own focus-visible heuristic says a *keyboard* focus ring
313	          // is warranted, which excludes a mouse-click-focused `<button>` in every evergreen
314	          // engine but still matches genuine Tab navigation — so the keyboard case Fix 2 exists
315	          // for keeps working, and the mouse-click case that produced the stuck-open bug does
316	          // not. `:has()` is not used anywhere else in this codebase yet; it is fully covered by
317	          // this project's own browserslist (`iOS >= 17`, `Android >= 14`, `last 4 ChromeAndroid
318	          // versions`), all far past `:has()`'s 2022/2023 shipping baseline. Expressed as a
319	          // separate string key (not a comma-joined `'&:hover, &:has(:focus-visible) ...'`
320	          // selector) to match this file's own established idiom; raw selector strings are used
321	          // throughout rather than a Chakra shorthand prop because the descendant-combinator
322	          // path has to be baked into the selector itself, and Chakra has no `:has()` shorthand.
323	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
324	            display: 'block',
325	          },
326	        }),
327	        ...(hoverHidesPrice && {
328	          // PLP/Wishlist: price is visible by default (no unconditional rule needed above) and
329	          // hides only here, in favour of the size-selector reveal alongside it.
330	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
331	            display: 'none',
332	          },
333	          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
334	          // Keyboard focus anywhere in the card must hide price in favour of the size-selector
335	          // exactly as hover does, so a keyboard user sees the identical revealed state, not a
336	          // different partial one; `:has(:focus-visible)` keeps that true while no longer
337	          // sticking open after a mouse click.
338	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
339	            display: 'none',
340	          },
341	        }),
342	        ...(hoverRevealsSizeSelector && {
343	          // ...and is only revealed here, matching the price swap alongside it.
344	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
345	            display: 'block',
346	          },
347	          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
348	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
349	            display: 'block',
350	          },
351	        }),
352	        // Fix C — see docblock point 4. Both the "hidden by default" declaration AND its reveal
353	        // live inside this same media-query block (unlike price/the size-selector above, whose
354	        // "hidden by default" half is unconditional): a touch pointer never matches this query at
355	        // all, so it never sees the `display: none` below either, leaving notify-me at its natural
356	        // (visible) default — exactly the unconditional visibility every Mobile Unavailable
357	        // reference confirms.
358	        ...(hoverRevealsNotifyMe && {
359	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
360	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
361	            display: 'block',
362	          },
363	          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
364	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
365	            display: 'block',
366	          },
367	        }),
368	
369	        // 6. Carousel arrow reveal — see docblock point 6. Unconditional (no
370	        // `ZimmProductCardStyleProps` flag gates it): desktop prev/next arrows behave identically
371	        // across every variation whenever a card has more than one image. Confirmed against the
372	        // Jira AC ("when on desktop and the user hovers, then the arrows appear") and live Figma:
373	        // the Carousel element is `hidden="true"` on every Default-state instance checked, visible
374	        // only on the matching Hover-state instance, for both PLP and Wishlist.
375	        // `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: { display: 'flex' }` used to
376	        // reveal this permanently on any hover-capable device (a device-capability check, not an
377	        // actual-hover one) — removed entirely there; this pair is now the only reveal path left,
378	        // the same `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` shape as the price/size-selector swap above.
379	        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
380	          display: 'flex',
381	        },
382	        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
383	          display: 'flex',
384	        },
385	      },
386	
387	      // 5. PLP-only bag-icon mobile hide — see docblock point 5. A separate, sibling media-query
388	      // key from HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY above (a viewport-width gate, not a pointer-capability one).
389	      // Mobile-first: hidden by default, shown again from the shared [DESKTOP_QUERY] block below.
390	      ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
391	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
392	      }),
393	
394	      // Fix F+D's shared desktop-reveal block — deliberately ONE `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object key,
395	      // not two. A first version of this recipe gave `sizeSelectorUnavailable` and
396	      // `hideBagOnMobile` each their OWN separate `...(condition && { [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {...} })`
397	      // spread (mirroring how every other flag in this file gets its own independent spread) —
398	      // which silently broke, because both spreads produce a property with the exact same
399	      // *computed key string* (`'@media (min-width: 48em)'`) on the same `root` object. Object
400	      // spread is a SHALLOW merge: it does not deep-merge two spreads that happen to share a key,
401	      // it just lets whichever spread comes LAST overwrite the earlier one's value entirely. With
402	      // `hideBagOnMobile`'s spread positioned after `sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s in this file, its
403	      // `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object silently replaced the other's, and the price-reveal-on-desktop
404	      // rule vanished from the actual emitted CSS — confirmed for real via
405	      // `document.styleSheets` in a live browser (price stayed `display: none` at 1280px width
406	      // despite `window.matchMedia('(min-width: 48em)').matches` correctly reporting `true`);
407	      // every jsdom test still passed, because each one only ever sets ONE of the two colliding
408	      // flags at a time, never the realistic combination a genuine unavailable PLP card produces.
409	      // `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` above never had this problem because it was always written as a
410	      // single key with every contributing condition spread INSIDE it — this block now follows
411	      // that same shape.
412	      [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {
413	        ...(sizeSelectorUnavailable && {
414	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: { display: 'block' },
415	        }),
416	        ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
417	          // 'flex', not 'block': ZimmProductCardContent's own `bagWrapper` part sets
418	          // `display: 'flex'` (it centres the icon inside via alignItems/justifyContent) — this
419	          // organism's `[data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="bag"]` selector has higher
420	          // specificity (a class + two attribute selectors vs. Content's own single class) and
421	          // would win the cascade either way, so restoring the actual display type Content uses
422	          // matters here, not just "anything visible" — 'block' would silently flatten that
423	          // wrapper's centering.
424	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'flex' },
425	        }),
426	      },
427	    },
428	  }),
429	};

import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { CARD_SLOT, HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY, DESKTOP_QUERY } from '../../zimmProductCardShared';

/**
 * Same hover-capable-pointer gate `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already establishes for its own
 * arrows/indicator split — now a shared import from `zimmProductCardShared.ts` rather than each
 * file's own module-private copy, so the two can't silently drift. Governs the price <->
 * size-selector swap below, so both composed children's hover treatments engage together off the
 * exact same media feature, on this shared root.
 */

/**
 * A viewport-width gate, unrelated to `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above — governs the PLP-only bag-icon
 * mobile hide (Fix D, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) below. Also a shared import from
 * `zimmProductCardShared.ts`, same reasoning as `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above: this and
 * `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`'s own `root` padding step both need the identical `min-width`
 * gate, and a module-private copy in each file was exactly the drift risk this extraction removes.
 */

type ZimmProductCardStyleProps = {
  /** Home only — see VARIATION_CONFIG in index.tsx. Price is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer
   *  type by default and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card. */

  sizeSelectorUnavailable?: boolean;

/**

 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` directly: neither its `root` nor `nameRow`, `nameLink`, or

 *          unconditionally. Every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference shows it appearing only on

 *          whatever it shows is the only state a touch pointer ever sees) shows it plainly with no

 *      reveal true — and the arrows visible — even after the mouse moved back out, until focus

 *      the card). The same shared-root `:focus-within` shape underlies every reveal in point 3

export const ZimmProductCard = {
  parts: ['root'],

  baseStyle: ({
    hoverHidesPrice,
    hoverRevealsPrice,
    hoverRevealsSizeSelector,
    hoverRevealsNotifyMe,
    sizeSelectorUnavailable,
    hideBagOnMobile,
  }: ZimmProductCardStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
    root: {
      position: 'relative',
      width: '100%',

      // 1. Stretched-link overlay — see docblock point 1. Deliberately no z-index of its own
      // (stays at the default/auto stacking layer), so every control lifted in point 2 below
      // reliably paints above it regardless of DOM order.
      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] a::after`]: {
        content: '""',
        position: 'absolute',
        inset: 0,
      },

      // 2. Every genuinely-interactive control sits above the stretched overlay. A plain `button`
      // type-selector under the relevant data-card-slot root reaches every control uniformly —
      // none of them declare their own data-card-slot, and none needs one: Content's bag button,
      // its notify-me button, and every ZimmSizeChip button nested inside its own sizeChips
      // wrapper are all real <button> descendants of [data-card-slot="content"].
      // Fix 1 (Scorer rework round 1): NO position value here. ZimmProductCardMedia's own

      // `.css-root [data-card-slot="close"]` descendant+attribute selector has HIGHER

      // here would win the cascade and knock the button out of its pinned position into normal
      // flow — which is exactly what shipped here before this fix. The element is already
      // positioned (by Media's own recipe), which is all `zIndex` needs to take effect; no
      // `position` re-declaration was ever necessary. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe
      // blocks for the object-shape and real-DOM/getComputedStyle proof.

        zIndex: 1,
      },
      // Fix 3 — zIndex only, on the carousel WRAPPER, not on each arrow `button` inside it. See
      // docblock point 2 above for why lifting the buttons individually left them unclickable in
      // a real browser (a `transform`-induced stacking context on this wrapper trapped their own
      // zIndex) despite passing every jsdom test.
      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
        zIndex: 1,
      },
      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] button`]: {
        position: 'relative',
        zIndex: 1,
      },

      // 3. Hover-reveal swap — see docblock point 3. The unconditional (outside-media-query)
      // half of each flag below is what makes a touch/no-hover pointer see the *default* state
      // permanently: it never matches HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY at all, so whichever rule fired outside
      // it (or the total absence of one) is the only state that pointer type ever sees.
      //
      // `hoverRevealsPrice` (Home) is deliberately NOT here, unlike `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`
      // below it — see Fix E in the [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY] block: Home's price must stay visible
      // unconditionally on a touch pointer, the opposite of what an unconditional hide here would
      // do.
      ...(hoverRevealsSizeSelector && {
        // PLP/Wishlist: size-selector starts hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type...
        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
      }),
      // Fix C — see docblock point 4. Unconditional and permanent, on every device: an
      // out-of-stock item never gets the size-selector, in any state, so this is the only rule
      // for it at all when `sizeSelectorUnavailable` is true (no corresponding reveal exists
      // anywhere, inside or outside the media query below).
      ...(sizeSelectorUnavailable && {
        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
        // Fix F (full-sweep follow-up audit): mobile-only price hide. Figma's Mobile PLP/Wishlist
        // Unavailable references hide price and show notify-me in its place — a genuine swap,
        // unlike Desktop's own additive treatment (price stays, notify-me is simply added on
        // hover, handled by hoverRevealsNotifyMe below). Hidden by default (mobile-first, matching
        // this file's own hideBagOnMobile direction); the DESKTOP_QUERY reveal lives in the single
        // shared [DESKTOP_QUERY] block below, NOT a second one here — see that block's own comment
        // for why a second `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object key at this level would silently clobber it.
        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: { display: 'none' },

      [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: {
        ...(hoverRevealsPrice && {
          // Fix E (full-sweep follow-up audit): the "hidden by default" half moved IN HERE from

          // here for the same underlying reason: a touch pointer must never see this half at all.

          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
            display: 'block',
          },
          // Fix 2 (Scorer rework round 1): `display: none` removes an element from the tab
          // order entirely, so a keyboard-only user on a hover-capable device (tabbing, not

          // stuck open, until focus moved elsewhere entirely (e.g. a click outside the card) —
          // moving the mouse back out was not enough. `:has(:focus-visible)` fixes this: it only

          // is warranted, which excludes a mouse-click-focused `<button>` in every evergreen

          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {

            display: 'block',
          },

        // Fix C — see docblock point 4. Both the "hidden by default" declaration AND its reveal

        // "hidden by default" half is unconditional): a touch pointer never matches this query at

        // reference confirms.
        ...(hoverRevealsNotifyMe && {
          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
            display: 'block',
          },
          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
            display: 'block',
          },
        }),

        // 6. Carousel arrow reveal — see docblock point 6. Unconditional (no
        // `ZimmProductCardStyleProps` flag gates it): desktop prev/next arrows behave identically
        // across every variation whenever a card has more than one image. Confirmed against the
        // Jira AC ("when on desktop and the user hovers, then the arrows appear") and live Figma:
        // the Carousel element is `hidden="true"` on every Default-state instance checked, visible
        // only on the matching Hover-state instance, for both PLP and Wishlist.
        // `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: { display: 'flex' }` used to
        // reveal this permanently on any hover-capable device (a device-capability check, not an
        // actual-hover one) — removed entirely there; this pair is now the only reveal path left,
        // the same `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` shape as the price/size-selector swap above.
        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
          display: 'flex',
        },
        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
          display: 'flex',
        },
      },

      // 5. PLP-only bag-icon mobile hide — see docblock point 5. A separate, sibling media-query
      // key from HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY above (a viewport-width gate, not a pointer-capability one).
      // Mobile-first: hidden by default, shown again from the shared [DESKTOP_QUERY] block below.
      ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
      }),

      // Fix F+D's shared desktop-reveal block — deliberately ONE `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object key,
      // not two. A first version of this recipe gave `sizeSelectorUnavailable` and
      // `hideBagOnMobile` each their OWN separate `...(condition && { [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {...} })`

      // which silently broke, because both spreads produce a property with the exact same
      // *computed key string* (`'@media (min-width: 48em)'`) on the same `root` object. Object

      // it just lets whichever spread comes LAST overwrite the earlier one's value entirely. With
      // `hideBagOnMobile`'s spread positioned after `sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s in this file, its

Step delivery was reconstructed directly from the 12 commits and the current code, verified by two independent whole-feature audits (`zm-orchestrator` for manifest-vs-diff, `zm-tester` for the internal/external sweep) plus direct spot-checks, not by trusting commit messages or plan.md's own claims about itself. ## Audit — findings.md (SFCC-236 rows only; SFCC-83/84 correctly stayed out of scope) | # | Gate item | Severity | Held? | Evidence | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Figma node ambiguity (6 candidate card components) | 🔴→cleared | **Held** | `40000223:2822` used consistently as the source of truth throughout plan.md and the shipped code's own citations | | 2 | Design-lock dates — Wishlist row at Sep 21, past PDP/Search&Rec's passed dates | 🔴→🟡 (wishlist only) | **Unaddressed, not re-checked** | Plan never revisits whether the Sep 21 Wishlist lock has since passed or was accepted as a pre-lock exception. Today is Sep 4 — the lock date hasn't arrived yet, so this isn't a violation, but nothing in plan.md or the shipped code records an explicit decision to build ahead of it. Worth a one-line confirmation before merge, not a blocker. | | 3 | Bag icon vs wishlist star (SPR-14 vs CRM-113) | 🔴→🟡 | **Held** | `Icon_bag` shipped, no wishlist heart anywhere in the card | | 8 | Badge delivery is a GET-hook field, absent from search/PLP grid responses; no story owns the gap | 🟡 CLARIFY | **Still open, correctly left to the mapper** | The card takes a pre-resolved `badge?: string` — it doesn't fetch or map data (container/presentational split), so this assumption was never this component's to resolve. The server-side gap TSD-225 flagged is exactly as open as before. Not a build defect. | | 9 | Wishlist needs colour+size, a "What's Now" price type, region-unavailable greyed state, destructive add-to-bag (CRM-137) | 🟡 CLARIFY | **Partially held** | Discriminated union with `colour`/`size`/required `onRemove` shipped as designed. Not found anywhere in the diff: a distinct "What's Now" price treatment, a region-unavailable greyed visual state, or `onAddToBag` behaving destructively for wishlist. `onRemove` is a separate, additive action, not a repurposed add-to-bag. Worth Marcel confirming these three were deliberately deferred (they look like page-level/data concerns, not card-rendering ones) rather than silently dropped. | | 10 | `product-tile/` override blast radius | 🟡 CLARIFY | **Held** | Confirmed not created, twice independently (orchestrator + tester), by direct `find`/grep | | 12 | Homepage may not be an SFCC-rendered component at all (Contentful) | 🟡 CLARIFY | **Carried forward without re-confirmation** | The build proceeded on `variation: 'home'` existing as a real card consumer. Nothing in plan.md's decision log (§4a–§4f) revisits whether Home is actually SFCC-rendered. Not a defect in what was built, but an assumption that was never closed out. | | 17 | Dani Rivett: no badge, no hover-image-swap on **Homepage or the Recently Viewed carousel** | 🟡 CLARIFY | **NOT held — see Sweep, this is the headline finding** | Only the Homepage half was implemented. See below. | | 18 | Recipe cannot be keyed `ProductTile` | 🔵 NOTE | **Held** | Key is literally `'ZimmProductCard'` | | 19 | VIC pricing needs a 3-state precedence rule | 🟡 CLARIFY | **Held, correctly deferred** | Plan explicitly punts to SFCC-778; card renders whatever price props it's given | | 21 | `overrideStyling.md` lines citing a nonexistent `product-tile/`/`CardBaseline` | 🔵 NOTE | **Still true, unrelated to this build** | Confirmed still absent; this is a pre-existing doc bug outside SFCC-236's scope to fix (per the finding's own note) | | 26 | Jira SFCC-743 "Product Card Group" may structurally duplicate the Recently Viewed rail | 🟡 CLARIFY | **Not addressed, correctly out of scope** | SFCC-236 doesn't build a rail — this stays a live question for whoever picks up SFCC-83/SFCC-743 | | 28 | "One component, four variants" framing exists in no Confluence doc | 🟡 CLARIFY | **Resolved by Marcel's own build-time authority** | The discriminated-union architecture in plan.md §4 *is* the resolution — recorded as a decision, not silently assumed | ## Audit — plan.md (via `zm-orchestrator`, whole-feature scope, tiers independently re-derived from CODEOWNERS/frozenFiles.md/protectedFiles.md — not trusted from the plan) | Step | Delivered? | Commit(s) | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | 1 — ZimmSlideIndicator | Yes | `27e5ea8` | Clamps correctly, `count≤1`→null, `role="group"`+computed `aria-label` (never `aria-hidden`, per the revised §4a criterion) | | 2 — ZimmSizeChip/Group | Yes | `9da4ad3` | §4d rename fully applied — zero `ZimmSizeSelector` references anywhere | | 3 — ZimmProductPrice `isLive` | Yes | `c00743f` | Additive-only, verified byte-for-byte | | 4 — ZimmProductCardMedia | Yes | `219d0a1`, `5802802`, `3793a01` | Badge/close/carousel/indicator all present; §4f's regression test for the height-alignment bug confirmed real | | 5 — ZimmProductCardContent | Yes | `79dcc67` | No badge/remove logic present — correctly lives in Media per §4c/§4f | | 6 — ZimmProductCard organism | Yes, with one unmet sub-criterion | `e999cee`, `5802802`, `ccc318d`, `9b8dc27`, `3793a01` | No `switch`/`if` on variation (confirmed by grep); two real `@ts-expect-error` cases (proven real — an unfired one would itself fail the clean `tsc --noEmit`); exactly one `` per card; **but** the "hover selector targets imported constants, not a string literal" criterion is not met — see UNIFORM finding below | | 7 — Gate and PR | Not yet reached | — | `tsc`/`test`/`audit:tokens` clean; no PR opened yet (correct — Hard Rule #15) | **Files in the diff not in the manifest — two findings, both directions:** - **UNDER-delivered:** `zimmProductCardShared.ts` (named explicitly in plan.md §3 and Step 6) was never created. See UNIFORM finding below. - **OVER-delivered:** `organisms/zimmProductCard/nodeCoverage/index.stories.tsx` (263 lines, new subfolder) was added by commit `38e29c0`, ~10.5 hours after the rest of the build finished. Its own commit message says it was built "per direct instruction" — this was an authorised, disclosed addition at the time, just never written back into plan.md's manifest (the same pattern as the Tier 1 `typography.ts` disclosure gap found and fixed earlier this session). `index.stories.tsx` itself also ships 8 exports against Step 6's named list of 7 (some renamed/folded, three genuinely new: `HomeOutOfStock`, `WishlistOutOfStock`, `MultipleImages`). Three extra `.css.test.ts` files exist beyond the plan's stated four-file-per-component template. None of this crosses a tier or owner — everything stays inside `ui-kits/`, both squads, Tier 3. **Tier re-derivation (independent of plan.md's own claims):** | File | Real tier (CODEOWNERS/frozenFiles.md/protectedFiles.md) | Matches plan's claim? | |---|---|---| | `theme/components/index.ts` | Tier 2 | Yes — clean append-only 6-entry addition | | `theme/foundation/typography.ts` | Tier 1 | Yes — disclosed mid-build correction, already confirmed authorised (marcelannavarro: tier-1-approvers + repo admin) | | `theme/globalStyles.ts` | Documented Tier 2 (protectedFiles.md), but **CODEOWNERS has no pattern actually matching this specific file** — a pre-existing enforcement gap in the repo, not introduced or worsened by this branch (which only changed 2 lines of an already-existing file) | Policy-correct, mechanically ungated — worth a separate ticket to Integration, not this PR's problem | | All 28 created files | Tier 3, both squads | Yes | Gate commands (re-run directly, not trusted from earlier in this session): `tsc --noEmit` clean · `npm run test` 54 files / 871 tests passing · `npm run lint` clean of every SFCC-236 file (5 remaining errors/18 warnings all pre-existing, outside this diff) · `audit:tokens` one pre-existing finding outside this diff (`footer.css.ts`), zero new findings — the one SFCC-236-authored raw value (`zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts:40`, `65px`) carries a compliant `audit-allow` comment. ## Sweep — internal consistency - **🔴 UNIFORM, confirmed by direct file absence + exhaustive grep — the promised single source of truth doesn't exist.** `zimmProductCardShared.ts` was never created. Consequence, verified directly: 10 distinct `data-card-slot` string literals are typed once in each producing molecule (`zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx`, `zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx`) and re-typed again as raw strings inside CSS selectors in `zimmProductCard.css.ts` (17+ occurrences) and again inside `querySelector(...)` calls across three test files. `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` (`'@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)'`) is independently defined in both `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` and `zimmProductCard.css.ts` — the latter's own docblock admits this is deliberate non-sharing. The only synchronisation mechanism anywhere is a comment reading *"Do not rename these values without updating that recipe too."* Both values currently agree, but nothing — no compiler, no lint rule, no test — would catch it if they stopped agreeing. This is precisely the drift risk `overrideStyling.md`'s "Cross-file shared values" section exists to prevent, and the plan cited the exact right precedent (`zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts`) for avoiding it. `CARD_BP` fares better — both consuming files import `breakpoints` directly from `theme/foundation`, a genuine single source, just not the named alias plan.md specified. - **🟡 UNIFORM, correctly-propagated pre-existing gap — no semantic "selected" border token exists.** `zimmSizeChip.css.ts` reaches for `var(--zimm-color-border-focus)` to mean "selected" (self-flagged in its own comment). Verified: `theme/foundation/colour.ts`'s border alias tier has no `selected`/`active` token at all, and the direct exemplar (`zimmColourSwatch.css.ts`) already does the identical thing with no caveat. This build correctly matched precedent rather than inventing a new pattern — the gap is a foundation-level should-fix (a `--zimm-color-border-selected` token), not a defect introduced here. - Every recipe otherwise matches shape (`parts` convention, registration pattern, `Zimm*` naming); every component matches the four/five-file structure; no value found typed three times in disagreement. ## Sweep — external conformance - **Against the exemplar** (`ZimmColourSwatch`/`ZimmColourSwatchGroup`, PR #64/#70) — matches on export/props naming, recipe-key pattern, file-set shape, and registration style. Roving-tabindex keyboard nav is independently re-implemented rather than shared (`handleChipsKeyDown` vs. `handleSwatchesKeyDown`) — a DRY tension, but consistent with this repo's own Hard Rule #5/#6 stance against refactoring upward into an already-shipped component. Not flagged as a defect. - **Against `.claude/rules/*`** — holds across the whole feature: token usage is `var(--zimm-*)` throughout with zero bare Chakra keys, imports are clean (no `../../../../` chains, no base-path shadowing, no later-sprint references), accessibility spot-checks (badge is genuinely non-interactive per §4c/§4f, close/arrows are real `

1	# SFCC-236 — Product Card Shared Component: Build Plan
2	
3	**Generated:** 2026-09-02 · **Planner:** `zm-planner` (Opus) · **Gate:** [findings.md](./findings.md)
4	**STATUS: GATE PASSED — ready for `zimmerMANNBuild`.** All blocking questions resolved; Tier 2 crossing approved
5	by Marcel 2026-09-02. Branch not yet cut (skill rule: never create a branch unasked).
6	**Scope: SFCC-236 only.** SFCC-83 and SFCC-84 are held — blocked on data source, surface list, and Legal's consent ruling.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## 1. Goal
11	
12	Build the shared Zimmermann Product Card per SFCC-236 (8 pts, Sprint 4, epic SFCC-2), designed in Figma
13	`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` set `40000223:2822` (20 variants: Size × State × Type × Unavailable), following the
14	FED handbook's ui-kits atomic layering and the PR #64 / `zimmColourSwatchGroup` pattern — named-export
15	component reading a `Zimm*`-namespaced multipart recipe via `useMultiStyleConfig`, parts applied with
16	`<chakra.div __css={styles.x}>`, all values `var(--zimm-*)` with explicit media queries.
17	
18	**The card is the visual layer only:** every value arrives as a prop, it owns no data fetching, and it renders
19	the add-to-bag / size-selection controls without wiring their behaviour (SFCC-185 / SFCC-497 / SFCC-90).
20	
21	---
22	
23	## 2. Scale call — one branch, seven commits, one PR
24	
25	```bash
26	git fetch origin && git checkout -b feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component origin/develop
27	```
28	
29	The current checkout (`feature/SFCC-91_...`) is merged and must not be built on.
30	
31	**Why one branch despite ~24 files:** one component family, one Figma set, one ticket, one reviewer set
32	(`pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b` on every file). The molecules have exactly one consumer — the organism — so
33	merging them separately merges dead code. Splitting would also multiply the single Tier 2 touch
34	(`theme/components/index.ts`) across three approval cycles for an append-only registry edit.
35	
36	**Full build loop (Implementer → Tester → Scorer per step).** This is a keystone blocking eight tickets, so a
37	wrong prop contract propagates into eight downstream stories.
38	
39	### Deliberately dropped
40	
41	| Dropped | Why |
42	|---|---|
43	| Copy-first | Nothing to copy — no file is being overridden at a mirrored path |
44	| Playwright / `.feature` | No page renders this component on this branch; E2E belongs to SFCC-80/90/497 |
45	| Bundle-size / LCP step | Nothing imports the card yet; bundle delta is zero |
46	| Visual regression | Chromatic/Loki is out of budget (`testing.md` excludes it); hover fidelity is a manual Storybook check |
47	| Multi-region fixtures | The card takes pre-formatted strings; no locale/currency logic to vary |
48	
49	**Retained, non-negotiable:** `npx tsc --noEmit` · `npm run test` · `npm run lint` · `npm run audit:tokens` ·
50	`cr review --light --base develop`.
51	
52	---
53	
54	## 3. File manifest
55	
56	### Modified (3 planned, 2 more added mid-build — see below)
57	
58	| File | Tier | Owner |
59	|---|---|---|
60	| `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` | **Tier 2** | `tier-2-approvers` + `tier-1-approvers` (CODEOWNERS:117) |
61	| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.tsx` | 3/4 | `pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b` |
62	| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.test.tsx` | 3/4 | same |
63	
64	**As planned, the Tier 2 file was the only tier crossing** and needed the explicit scope
65	confirmation AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 requires before Step 1 — obtained, see the STATUS line.
66	
67	**Superseded by mid-build discovery (2026-09-04):** Step 5's commit `f775026` additionally
68	touched two files never in this manifest and never surfaced as a tier crossing at the time:
69	
70	| File | Tier | Owner | Why |
71	|---|---|---|---|
72	| `overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts` | **Tier 1** | UI Designer | `linkSm.textTransform` was `capitalize` in both this file and its `globalStyles.ts` mirror, disagreeing with Figma node `40002163:41468` ("NOTIFY ME", fully capitalised) — a pre-existing drift, not a new value invented for this card. Corrected to `uppercase` in both places so the theme collision-guard test (`theme/index.test.tsx`) passes and Step 5's notify-me link renders correctly. |
73	| `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts` | Tier 2 | UI Designer | The `.zimm-text-link-sm` mirror of the same token — see "The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy" in `overrideStyling.md`; corrected in lockstep so the two can't disagree again. |
74

80	admin, so per the verified-session exception in AGENTS.md's Tier 1 Approval section, proceeding

84	"no Tier 1 file is touched," which is no longer true.
85

87

91	molecules/zimmSlideIndicator/
92	atoms/zimmSizeChip/

94	molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/

96	organisms/zimmProductCard/          + zimmProductCardShared.ts
97	```
98

100	PLP, Search, Home, Cart, PDP and empty-search-results, and `product-list/index.jsx:51-53` imports

102	
103	`zimmProductCardShared.ts` holds DOM-contract constants (`data-card-slot` names). No design values, so it
104	was originally co-located with the organism (precedent: `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts`).
105	
106	**Corrected 2026-09-04 (postbuild Round 3, commit `0f35e0c`):** that co-location was wrong for this file's
107	actual consumers. Unlike `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts` — imported only by its one owning molecule —
108	this file is imported by two *sibling* molecules (`zimmProductCardMedia`, `zimmProductCardContent`), which
109	had to reach up into the organism's own folder to get it. Relocated to `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/`
110	directly — a genuine common ancestor, not owned by any one of the three components — and every import path

114	
115	**A second file, added later in the same pattern, was found, fixed, then un-extracted entirely
116	(2026-09-04, Round 6) — its full history, for the record:** `organisms/zimmProductCard/productCardFixtures.ts`
117	(added Round 3, commit `5b49864`) held Storybook-only fixture data plus a demo wrapper component, imported
118	by the same two sibling molecules from the same backward direction `zimmProductCardShared.ts` was fixed
119	for. Its docblock cited `overrideStyling.md`'s "SFCC bridge pattern" section as justification — that
120	section says nothing about Storybook fixtures; the citation was fabricated (Round 4 finding). Rather than

125	each piece restored locally to whichever file(s) actually use it, including a second, independently

127	**`zimmProductCardShared.ts` is the one file this reasoning still supports** — it stays at `ui-kits/` root.
128	
129	**Manifest count correction:** four files exist with no citation in this section, all added mid-build and
130	disclosed only in their own commit messages: `zimmSizeChip.css.test.ts`, `zimmSizeChipGroup.css.test.ts`,

135	
136	**Superseded 2026-09-05 (commit `02a3203`):** `nodeCoverage/index.stories.tsx`, cited above, no longer
137	exists. Marcel asked for the two separate Storybook surfaces (this file's own curated stories plus that

147	live total.
148	
149	---
150	
151	## 4. Architecture decisions
152	
153	**Variation axis = discriminated union (data contract) + declarative config table (layout).**
154	`typescript.md` mandates the union, and the ACs require it: Wishlist alone needs `colour` + `size` + mandatory
155	`onRemove`; PLP alone needs `sizes` + `onNotifyMe`. A flat optional-everything bag lets you build a Wishlist
156	card with no remove CTA (AC violation) and a PLP card with one (design violation).
157	
158	```
159	ZimmProductCardProps = Base & (PlpVariation | HomeVariation | WishlistVariation)
160	  base:       id, href, name, headingLevel, primaryImage, hoverImage?, images?,
161	              currentPrice?, originalPrice?, isUnavailable?, badge?
162	  'plp':      sizes?, selectedSize?, onSizeSelect?, onAddToBag?, onNotifyMe?
163	  'home':     —
164	  'wishlist': colour, size, onRemove (required), onAddToBag?
165	```
166	
167	`'recently-viewed'` is **not** a fourth member — the AC says it behaves identically to PLP, so consumers pass
168	`variation: 'plp'`. Recorded as an assumption, not a silent choice.
169	
170	The render body must **not** `switch` on `props.variation`. Layout comes from a module-level `VARIATION_CONFIG`
171	(`showBag`, `showAttributes`, `showRemove`, `hoverHidesPrice`, `hoverRevealsPrice`, `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`,
172	`hoverSwapsImage`). That is what satisfies the extensibility AC: add a union member + a config row, touch no JSX.
173	
174	**The card is fluid, not 288px.** `gridSystem.ts` has `maxWidth: 'none'`. Figma's 288/179 are widths at the
175	reference artboards. The card fills its grid cell (`width: 100%`); the image holds ratio via `aspectRatio`.
176	Grid placement belongs to SFCC-80.
177	
178	**Mobile/desktop boundary = 768px** (`breakpoints.md`, 48em) — the only confirmed foundation breakpoint between
179	the 402 and 1440 artboards, and where the grid already goes 4→8 columns. `min-width` is inclusive, so the 768
180	artboard gets the desktop card. Every hover rule is additionally gated on `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`
181	so a 768px touch tablet never gets hover-only content. See OQ-5.
182	
183	**Hover is CSS-only, keyed on `:hover, :focus-within`.** No React hover state — 60 tiles re-rendering on pointer
184	move is a PLP perf defect. `:focus-within` is not optional: WCAG 2.2 AA requires the revealed size selector and
185	arrows be keyboard-reachable. All reveal selectors live in one place, the organism's recipe root part, selecting
186	descendants by the shared `data-card-slot` constants. Molecules stay hover-agnostic.
187	
188	**One link per card (stretched-link).** The card holds a bag button, arrows, size options and a remove button —
189	nesting those in an `<a>` is invalid HTML and an a11y failure. The link wraps the product name only and carries
190	a `::after { position:absolute; inset:0 }` overlay; controls get `position:relative; z-index:1`. `href` arrives
191	pre-prefixed from the page. Uses `import {Link as RouteLink} from 'react-router-dom'` per `zimmColourSwatch` —
192	there is no `overrides/app/components/link/` override, contrary to a claim in `overrideStyling.md`.
193	
194	**Reuse, don't rebuild:** `ZimmProductName`, `ZimmProductPrice`, `ZimmIcon` (`bag`, `close`, `chevron-left`,
195	`chevron-right` all exist in `ICON_MAP`). No new icons.
196	
197	**VIC pricing is not a card concern** — precedence is the page mapper's job. Deferred to SFCC-778 (OQ-6).
198	
199	---
200	
201	## 4a. Arrows vs. indicator — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02)
202	
203	> *"position indicator is just for tablet and mobile, desktop hover is arrows"*
204	
205	The two are **mutually exclusive**, not paired. Consequences for Steps 1 and 4:
206	
207	**Split by pointer capability, not viewport width.** The gate is
208	`@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` — the same gate every other hover rule already uses:
209	
210	- **hover-capable + fine pointer** → prev/next arrow buttons, revealed on `:hover, :focus-within`. No indicator.
211	- **everything else (touch tablet, mobile)** → `ZimmSlideIndicator`, always visible. No arrows.
212	
213	Capability rather than width is what actually delivers the stated intent: the 768 artboard is a *touch* tablet,
214	and a width rule alone would give it arrows it can never hover to reveal. It also keeps this consistent with the
215	card's own hover rules rather than introducing a second, differently-keyed breakpoint. **Edge case, accepted:**
216	a desktop browser resized below 768 keeps arrows (it still has a fine pointer); a touch-screen laptop gets the
217	indicator. Both are the safe failure direction — nobody is shown a control they cannot operate.
218	
219	**Two knock-on changes to the step pass criteria:**
220	
221	1. **Step 1 — the indicator is NOT `aria-hidden` on touch.** The original criterion assumed the arrow buttons
222	   announce position, so the indicator could be hidden as duplicate. Where the indicator renders there are **no

231	## 4b. Touch image paging — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02)
232	
233	> *"scroll-snap it is"*
234	
235	Native CSS scroll-snap. The dots remain a **passive readout**, visually unchanged from Figma — no enlargement,
236	no conversion to tap targets, so no departure from the design and no WCAG 2.5.8 problem to solve.
237	
238	**Implementation shape: one scroll container on every breakpoint, not two mechanisms.**
239	
240	The image strip is always a horizontally scrollable flex container with `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` and
241	`scrollSnapAlign: 'start'` on each slide. What differs by pointer capability is only the *affordance* layered
242	over it:
243	
244	| | Mechanism | Affordance |
245	|---|---|---|
246	| hover + fine pointer | same scroll container | arrows call `scrollBy()`; no indicator |
247	| touch | same scroll container | native drag; indicator reflects position |
248	
249	One container rather than two code paths means a single source of truth for "which image is showing", the
250	arrows become progressive enhancement over something that already works, and the desktop path inherits
251	keyboard scrollability for free.
252	
253	**Active-index derivation:** prefer `IntersectionObserver` on the slides over a scroll listener — 60 tiles on a
254	PLP make a per-scroll-event listener a real perf cost, and the repo already has
255	`overrides/app/hooks/use-intersection-observer.ts` (**Tier 2 — import it, do not modify it**). The `scrollend`
256	event is an acceptable alternative. Left to the Implementer; either satisfies the pass criteria.
257	
258	**Precedent:** the base `ProductScroller`
259	(`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-scroller/index.jsx:79-84`) already uses
260	`scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` with `overflowX: 'scroll'`. Same technique, already proven in this codebase.
261	
262	**Accepted caveat:** swipe has no explicit affordance beyond the dots implying further content. This is the
263	universal mobile convention, and the alternative (enlarging 1px dots into 24×24 tap targets) trades an
264	invisible-but-expected gesture for a visible-but-off-design control. **Action: flag to Kiera that the mobile
265	gesture is undocumented in the design**, so it lands in the spec rather than being discovered in QA.
266	
267	**Added Step 4 pass criteria:**
268	- The slide container carries `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'`; every slide carries `scrollSnapAlign`.
269	- Arrows are rendered only under `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`; the indicator only outside it; assert the
270	  two never coexist in the same DOM.
271	- Arrow activation moves the scroll position (assert `scrollBy`/`scrollTo` is called — jsdom does not lay out,
272	  so assert the call, not the resulting offset).
273	- The indicator's active index tracks the observed slide, and clamps at both ends.
274	- A single-image product renders no indicator, no arrows, and no horizontal overflow.
275	- No gesture library is added — `package.json` is untouched (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7).
